Symbolic and numerical derivatives of the same function, checked against each
other. Attach the kernel with `<leader>ji`, then run a cell with `<leader>jr`.

```{python}
%matplotlib inline

import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import sympy as sp

sp.init_printing(use_unicode=True)
```

`f(x) = e^{-x²} sin(3x)` — sympy differentiates it in closed form.

```{python}
x = sp.symbols("x")
f = sp.exp(-(x**2)) * sp.sin(3 * x)
df = sp.diff(f, x)
df
```

JAX differentiates the same function by tracing it, with no closed form
involved. `vmap` lifts the scalar derivative to the whole grid.

```{python}
def f_jax(x):
    return jnp.exp(-(x**2)) * jnp.sin(3 * x)


grid = jnp.linspace(-3, 3, 400)
df_jax = jax.vmap(jax.grad(f_jax))(grid)
```

Agreement to floating-point tolerance is the real test that both paths describe
the same function.

```{python}
df_sym = sp.lambdify(x, df, "numpy")(np.asarray(grid))
np.max(np.abs(df_sym - np.asarray(df_jax)))
```

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3.5))
ax.plot(grid, f_jax(grid), label="f")
ax.plot(grid, df_jax, label="f′ (jax)")
ax.plot(grid, df_sym, "--", label="f′ (sympy)")
ax.legend()
ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
plt.show()
```
